subtype: Stage 6: One-on-one time and joint tasks [Response]
passage:
"Leela, it's your special time now. Just you and me. What shall we do?"
"Can we read the elephant book? Only us?"
"Only us. Seema is with Appa."
After ten minutes, Amma called, "Seema, your turn!"
"Amma, can we do puzzle?"
"Yes, kanna."
Later, Amma put a big cardboard box on the floor. "Can you two make a house together?"
"I'll do the door!" said Leela.
"I'll do windows!" said Seema.
"Help me hold this, Seema!"
"Okay, akka!"
Amma smiled. They didn't fight once.

qa.q: What did Leela want to read in her special time?
qa.a: She wanted to read the elephant book, just with Amma.

qa.q: How can you tell Leela was happy about her special time?
qa.a: She asked "Only us?" eagerly, showing she loved having Amma to herself.

qa.q: Why does the cardboard house work well after special time?
qa.a: Each child already feels sure of Amma's attention, so building together feels fun and they help each other instead of fighting.

qa.q: How might Seema feel helping her akka build the house?
qa.a: She likely feels proud and happy to be working with Leela. 😊

grounding: It shows each child getting a short time alone with the parent and then building something together, which eases rivalry.

passage:
Note on the fridge, from Manjula, for Appa.
Week two of our plan: 10 minutes alone with each child every evening. Devika (6) chose to paint with me. Kartik (4) chose rolling a ball. Both waited their turn without fighting.
Today they built a train from shoe boxes together. Devika held the tape, Kartik stuck on wheels. Kartik said, "Akka, we're a team!" Devika laughed.
Fewer fights this week. 🎉

qa.q: What did Kartik choose to do in his time alone?
What does Kartik's "Akka, we're a team!" show about his feelings?
qa.a: It shows he feels happy and proud working with his sister, and enjoys being on her side.

qa.q: Why might the plan be reducing fights?
qa.a: Each child gets reliable time alone, so they feel sure of their place, and building the train shows them that working together feels good.

qa.q: How might Devika see her little brother now?
qa.a: She may see Kartik more as a teammate than a rival, laughing with him as they build.

grounding: It illustrates each child getting short daily time alone with a parent and building something together, easing rivalry through security and cooperation.
